For masked positions M_b, per-target loss is Σ_bΣ_{t∈M_b}ℓ_bt / Σ_b|M_b|; per-sequence loss is mean_b[Σ_tℓ_bt/|M_b|]. The former weights sequences by mask count, typically favoring longer retained histories; the latter gives each sampled sequence equal weight. Reproducible examples: original [BERT4Rec](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py) uses weighted target averaging; [PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/jaywonchung/BERT4Rec-VAE-Pytorch/blob/master/trainers/bert.py) flattens logits and applies CrossEntropyLoss(ignore_index=0). Derived implication: choosing an entire batch’s branch with probability 0.5 and normalizing each batch preserves a 50:50 expected branch objective. Pooling targets across mixed-branch sequences instead gives random masking approximately E|M|/(E|M|+1) weight. Guarantee at least one mask to avoid undefined sequence means.

Sampling derivation: let n_u be training-history length and m≥1 minimum context length; eligible target indices are t=m,…,n_u−1, totaling K_u=n_u−m. Uniform user then uniform endpoint gives P(u,t)=1/(U K_u); uniform over all endpoints gives 1/Σ_uK_u, favoring users with more endpoints. Increasing m excludes early transitions and short-history users, changing item exposure; neither policy eliminates popularity bias. Reproducible recipe: rng.choice(eligible_users), then rng.integers(m,n_u); input leftpad((history[:t]+[MASK])[-L:]), target history[t]. Reserve the mask token and read position −1. [BERT dataloader](https://github.com/jaywonchung/BERT4Rec-VAE-Pytorch/blob/master/dataloaders/bert.py) demonstrates reserved-mask, left-padding and appended-mask inference.

Full-catalog cross-entropy avoids negative-proposal weighting. With sampled BCE, ℓ=−logσ(s_y)−Σ_{k=1}^K logσ(−s_jk), expected negative pressure scales as Kq(j); popularity/in-batch proposals penalize frequent negatives more often, while uniform proposals do not remove positive-frequency bias. Averaging versus summing negatives changes that balance. Corrected sampled-softmax is a distinct approximation: use proposal-aware expected counts and accidental-hit handling, as in [TensorFlow’s implementation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss). Exclusions alter q; never consult held-out labels.
